$what: Provenance of aurora-regions.schema.json, empyrean's CONTRACT schema for an act's regions document, vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. document.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/regions-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_only_a_test_const: Because nothing hashes a comment. The scene schema's pin lived as a `const` in its drift test and as prose in two more files, and the prose copy went THREE re-pins stale without anything going red. The hash lives HERE, once, machine readable, and the test reads it. Every prose citation of a hash in this repo, including the ones in this file's own pin history, is prose and says so.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path probe design would degrade to 'schema not found, so skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate and the currency check are the payment. This file is never read from a sibling checkout at runtime or at test time by path, only through git objects at a named revision (docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md is the defect that made reading a peer's LIVE WORKING TREE unacceptable).
$why_not_under_test_fixtures: This is a SOURCE file the app imports, not a test fixture, so it lives beside its consumer. The same reason the scene and preset schemas do: the published-revision sweep in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts walks test/fixtures/ and reads a `revision` key inside a block it knows; a schema the RENDERER needs at runtime cannot live under test/ at all, whatever the sweep does.

what_this_pin_carries: THE FIRST VENDORING OF THIS FILE, so there is no diff to read and the thing worth recording is what arrived. The document is closed at THREE levels, not one (the root, a region, and `bg`), which is the property vector 10 exists to prove. It brings exactly ONE keyword json-schema-subset.ts did not implement, and that was MEASURED with collectSchemaKeywords over the vendored bytes rather than guessed from the candidate list in the dispatch: `maxLength`, at /$defs/region/properties/name. Every other candidate named there (const, $ref with $defs, unevaluatedProperties, pattern, minItems, the union type [string, null], minimum) was ALREADY implemented and needed nothing. `maxLength` is the first bound in either committed contract schema on FREE AUTHOR PROSE rather than on an identifier: every string bound before it was a regex carrying its own {0,31} repetition count, and a label nobody parses has no pattern to hang a count on. Implemented over CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units, so an astral character in an author's label counts once as the spec says and not twice as String.prototype.length would.
the_hole_this_pin_carries: `bg.span` is DERIVED FROM THE REFERENCED LAYOUT AND NEVER TYPED BY HAND (part 2 section 6.2 item 1), and NO KEYWORD IN THIS FILE CAN SAY SO. The schema asserts only 'integer, at least 1'; Aurora's codec has no background layout library yet, so a hand-edited span that disagrees with the layout `bg.layoutRef` names is accepted here, round-tripped unchanged, and left for the generator to catch. Recorded as a hole rather than left as a silence, because a schema that validates the key reads as a schema that checks it. The schema's own description lists four more of the same kind: that `preset` names a record that exists, that `layoutRef` names a layout in the library, that a rectangle lies inside the act, and that the union of referenced layouts fits BG_TILE_CAPACITY.
